URL: https://potatoannotator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/releasenotes/v2.8.2/

# Release Notes: v2.8.2 — The Fixes 2.8.1 Said It Had

**2.8.1 did not contain two of the five fixes its release notes and advisories
described.** The SSRF fix and the debug-mode hardening were never written. The
release notes for them were. Anyone who upgraded to 2.8.1 for either issue was
not protected, and the advisories said they were.

That is a documentation failure with a security consequence, and it is worse
than shipping nothing, because it told people to stop worrying.

```bash
pip install --upgrade potato-annotation
```

## Fix status by release

| Issue | Advisory | In 2.8.1 | In 2.8.2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| RCE through the live coding agent | `GHSA-cm4p-5rfv-x252` | Yes | Yes |
| Admin config readable without the key | — | Yes | Yes |
| Trace-ingestion webhook accepted everyone | — | Yes | Yes |
| SSRF on the media endpoints | `GHSA-9394-85jj-2mhj` | **No** | Yes |
| Debug mode on a reachable interface | `GHSA-r4ww-vc5h-35qf` | **No** | Yes |

The three that were real in 2.8.1 are unchanged. If you are on 2.8.1 and do not
use audio or video annotation and never enable `debug`, you are no worse off
than you thought. Otherwise, upgrade.

## SSRF on the media endpoints

Four endpoints took a URL from the caller and fetched it server-side:
`/api/audio/proxy`, `/api/waveform/generate`, `/api/video/waveform/generate` and
`/api/video/metadata`. None required a login. The proxy returned the response
body, so it read anything the server could reach — cloud instance metadata,
loopback-bound admin interfaces, internal APIs. The waveform endpoints do not
return the body, but they fetch what they are given, and when the input was not
a URL they treated it as a local path and passed it to a subprocess, which
answered whether an arbitrary path existed on the host.

All four now require a login, and every URL goes through one shared guard in
`potato/server_utils/url_guard.py`. It:

- allows only `http` and `https`
- resolves the host and refuses loopback, private, link-local, reserved,
  multicast, unspecified, CGNAT and cloud-metadata addresses, including their
  IPv6 and v4-mapped spellings
- refuses a host that resolves to *any* blocked address, rather than picking a
  public one from a mixed answer — a name that answers with both is a rebinding
  primitive, not a host with a fallback
- connects to the address it validated instead of handing the name back to
  `requests`, which would resolve it a second time
- re-validates every redirect hop, since a public URL that redirects to the
  metadata service defeats any check of the caller's URL alone
- caps the response, both on the declared Content-Length and while reading
- **fails closed** on a name that will not resolve. The old `web_proxy`
  validator allowed that case on the reasoning that the fetch would fail
  anyway. It does not: a name that fails once can answer on the retry.

The audio proxy no longer sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Every caller
is the annotation page on the same origin, and the wildcard let any site read
proxied content through a logged-in user's browser.

Local paths handed to waveform generation now resolve inside `task_dir`, with
`realpath` containment that catches `..` and symlinks pointing out.

If you genuinely need the server to fetch from an internal host, name it in
`media_url_allowlist`.

## Debug mode

`debug: true` disabling admin authentication is deliberate and documented. It
was also unconditional, and the default bind is `0.0.0.0`.

- The admin bypass applies only when the server is bound to loopback. On any
  other interface, debug grants nothing and the admin key is still required.
- The server refuses to start with `debug: true` on a non-loopback bind. Set
  `POTATO_ALLOW_REMOTE_DEBUG=1` if you accept the risk; the error names that.
- The Werkzeug interactive debugger is never served off loopback, override or
  not. Potato's debug conveniences and Flask's remote console are now separate
  things.
- The admin dashboard puts the admin key in its HTML only for a caller who
  already presented it. Under the debug bypass or an RBAC role the caller never
  supplied the key, and emitting it there handed the real key to anyone who
  could load the page.
- Startup says what debug is doing: which interface, whether the bypass is
  active, whether the debugger is on.

Local debugging against `127.0.0.1` is unchanged, and `potato preview` now
binds its throwaway server to loopback, which it should always have done.

## Cause of the incomplete 2.8.1 release

The 2.8.1 work implemented one phase of a five-phase remediation plan and then
wrote release notes for all five. The verification that ran afterwards checked
the version number and the phase that had been built, so it passed.

The check that would have caught it — asserting each claimed fix against the
built artifact — is now in the test suite rather than in a checklist:
`tests/unit/test_url_guard.py`, `tests/unit/test_debug_bind_guard.py` and
`tests/server/test_media_proxy_ssrf.py`. The last of those asserts both that an
unauthenticated caller is refused **and** that an authenticated one still cannot
reach an internal address, because every annotator on a crowdsourced task is
authenticated and a test that only checks the first proves very little.

<!-- source: docs/releasenotes/v2.8.1.md -->
URL: https://potatoannotator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/releasenotes/v2.8.1/

# Release Notes: v2.8.1 — Security Fixes

> **Correction, 2026-08-26:** this page originally described five fixes. Two of
> them — the SSRF fix and the debug-mode hardening — were **not in 2.8.1**. They
> shipped in [2.8.2](v2.8.2.md). The sections below are left as published, with
> this note, rather than quietly rewritten. If you upgraded to 2.8.1 for either
> issue, upgrade again.

A patch release. It closes five security issues, three of them reported
privately against 2.8.0 through GitHub's advisory flow, and two found while
fixing those. **Upgrade if you run Potato anywhere other than localhost.**

```bash
pip install --upgrade potato-annotation
```

## The five issues

### Unauthenticated SSRF through the media endpoints

`/api/audio/proxy` took a URL from the query string, fetched it server-side, and
returned the body to the caller. The only check was that the URL started with
`http://` or `https://`. There was no authentication, so anyone who could reach
the port could ask the server to fetch anything it could reach — a cloud
instance's metadata service, an internal admin UI, a service on the LAN — and
read the response back.

`/api/waveform/generate` and `/api/video/waveform/generate` had the same shape.
They do not return the body, but they fetch what they are given, and when the
input is not a URL they treat it as a local path and hand it to a subprocess,
which answers "does this file exist" for any path on the host.

All four now require a login and validate the URL through one shared guard that
resolves the host, refuses private, loopback, link-local, reserved and cloud
metadata addresses, pins the connection to the address it validated so the name
cannot be re-resolved to another one, re-checks every redirect hop, and caps the
response size. `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` is gone from the proxy; every
caller was same-origin.

Three URL validators already existed in the codebase and none of them was
shared. They are now one, and the weakest of those behaviours is gone: a host
that fails to resolve is no longer allowed through.

*Reported privately. Credit in the advisory.*

### Remote code execution through the live coding agent

Every route in the live coding agent blueprint started, instructed, rolled back
or stopped a real agent session, and none of them checked for a login. The
global session gate did not cover them either: it exempts the bare `/api/`
prefix, so it never ran for anything in that blueprint.

From there, `POST /api/live_coding_agent/replay/<session_id>` accepted
`edited_actions`, tool calls supplied by the caller, and executed them.
`Bash` ran through `subprocess.run(shell=True)` on the host, and `Read`, `Write`
and `Edit` honoured absolute paths by construction, so they reached any file the
Potato user could.

The sandbox that was supposed to contain this did not. `sandbox_mode: docker`
was never implemented: it logged a warning and fell back to running tools
directly on the host, so an operator who asked for a container got nothing and
was not told. The default, `worktree`, is a git worktree on the same host, as the same
user, with the same network. It was documented as "safe isolation".

Fixed in three layers. Every route requires a login and checks that the session
belongs to the caller. Client-supplied `working_dir`, `backend_type` and
`ai_config` are ignored; those come from the server's config only. And the
sandbox was rebuilt as a real one, described below.

*Reported privately. Credit in the advisory.*

### Admin config readable without the admin key

The admin config endpoint authorized its POST branch and not its GET branch, so
any caller could read the task configuration back, including whatever
credentials and endpoint settings it held. The read side now requires the same
key the write side always did.

Found while writing tests for the reports above. The test harness had been
sending a hardcoded admin key that only worked because debug mode accepts
anything, so the admin tests had been exercising the debug bypass rather than
the real check, which is why this went unnoticed.

### Trace-ingestion webhook accepted everyone

`WebhookReceiver.authenticate()` returned true whenever `trace_ingestion.api_key`
was unset. Turning trace ingestion on without also setting a key left an
unauthenticated endpoint that writes items into the annotation task. Enabling a
feature should not be the same act as disabling its authentication.

It now fails closed. An operator who wants an open receiver on a trusted network
sets `allow_unauthenticated: true` and says so, and Potato warns at startup
either way.

### Debug mode on a reachable interface

`debug: true` disables admin authentication by design and is documented that
way. What was not obvious is how the pieces combine: the default bind is
`0.0.0.0`, the admin dashboard put the real admin key into the rendered HTML,
and Flask's debugger is an interactive console for anyone who can reach it.

Debug remains a local convenience. It no longer grants admin on a non-loopback
bind, the server refuses to start with debug on a public interface unless
`POTATO_ALLOW_REMOTE_DEBUG=1` is set, the admin key is out of the HTML, and the
Werkzeug debugger is never handed to a non-loopback bind. Deployment preflight
already refused debug and still does.

*Reported privately. Credit in the advisory.*

## The new sandbox ladder

Annotators can edit an agent's tool call and re-run it. That is the point of the
feature, so the boundary those tools run inside is the security control. It is
now a ladder, and you pick the rung your machine supports:

| `sandbox_mode` | Boundary | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `container` (default) | Namespaces, cgroups, seccomp | `docker` or `podman` |
| `container` + `container_runtime` | gVisor or a hardware VM | `runsc` or `kata` installed |
| `bubblewrap` | Namespaces, no daemon, no root | `bwrap`, Linux |
| `trusted` | None | An explicit acknowledgement |

Containers run with no network, a read-only root filesystem, as `nobody`, with
every capability dropped and limits on memory, CPU and process count. The agent
works on a per-session copy of `working_dir`, never the directory itself.

Nothing here implements isolation from scratch. Each rung drives a tool that
already does, which is also why the strongest options are configuration rather
than code: gVisor and Kata install as drop-in container runtimes, so
`container_runtime: runsc` upgrades the boundary with no change on Potato's
side. `container_cli: podman` gets rootless containers, which need no root
daemon.

`bubblewrap` is there for shared machines and clusters where Docker is not
available and rootless Podman is impractical. It is a weaker boundary and says
so at startup.

**Backends never fall back.** If the one you configured is unavailable, the
session fails with an error naming the alternatives, and the check runs at
startup rather than at the first tool call. Silently degrading to no isolation
is the defect this replaces.

## Breaking changes

**`sandbox_mode` defaults to `container`.** If you run the live coding agent
without Docker or Podman, Potato will not start until you choose a rung. The
error names all three ways forward.

**`worktree` and `direct` now require an acknowledgement.** Both map to
`trusted` and need `acknowledge_untrusted_code_execution: true` alongside:

```yaml
live_coding_agent:
  sandbox_mode: trusted
  acknowledge_untrusted_code_execution: true
```

This will stop existing configs from starting, which is deliberate. `worktree`
was the default and read as isolation; against a shell it provides none. It is
still worth having for keeping agent edits off your main checkout, and it is
still available. It just no longer claims to be a boundary.

**`output_annotation_format` is deprecated.** It has not been read since the v2
storage rewrite, so it was configuring nothing. It now folds onto
`export_annotation_format` with a warning, and `potato migrate` converts it.

## Also in this release

- The three universal sidebars are gated server-side, so a plain task stops
  making six failed background requests per page.
- Quality-control items no longer count against an annotator's quota, which was
  ending studies with articles still unannotated.
- A required scheme hidden by `display_logic` no longer blocks saving.
- Sixteen schema types landed outside the `layout.groups` group they were
  assigned to; they now land inside it.
- `on:` in a config is read as a key rather than as YAML 1.1's boolean `True`.
- Potato warns when a scheme is renamed out from under existing annotations,
  which previously showed as 100% complete with zero agreement.
- An MCP server, a browser-backed `potato preview --screenshot`, and a
  machine-readable catalog of the shipped examples, so coding agents can check
  their work instead of guessing.
- `potato deploy local` and `potato deploy share`, and bundle directories scoped
  per provider. A cloud rebuild used to clean out the directory a local
  deployment was writing into.

## Credits

Three of these were reported privately and responsibly through GitHub's advisory
flow, with clear reproductions and suggested fixes. Named in the advisories.

<!-- source: docs/releasenotes/v2.8.0.md -->

# Release Notes: v2.8.0 — Vision, and the Statistics to Check It

36 commits, 1,145 files, ~205,000 lines added since v2.7.1. Most of it is one
project: rebuilding Potato's image, video, 3D, embodied and world-model
surfaces, which had been a thin layer over the text annotation machinery. The rest is threaded
conversations and ConvoKit, keystroke logging, live database ingestion,
machine-readable specs for coding agents, and a repair pass on the packaging,
performance and offline-install problems found along the way.

Two things to read before upgrading: **image annotation keyboard shortcuts have
changed by default** (§Upgrading), and if you install from PyPI rather than
from a checkout, **2.7.1 and earlier shipped a broken wheel** (§Packaging).

## Agreement over geometry and time

The headline, and the part with no equivalent elsewhere: Potato reports
**chance-corrected agreement over shapes, and over the moment something
happened**. Existing tools compare geometry with a raw IoU threshold, which
does not correct for chance and says nothing about polylines, keypoints or
temporal boundaries.

Agreement decomposes, because the disagreement does. Annotators can differ on
whether an object is there at all, on what to call it, and on where its edge
lies, and those have different fixes:

- **detection** — did they find the same objects (nominal α over presence)
- **localization** — given a match, do they agree where it is
- **classification** — given a match, do they agree what it is
- **geometry scale** — reported as a σ (typical disagreement in image widths)
  and a KS test, rather than a single coefficient that hides the distribution

Masks add STAPLE (Warfield et al. 2004) for a latent consensus boundary with
per-rater sensitivity and specificity — the medical-imaging analogue of MACE,
used because MACE models a finite shared label set and a mask does not have
one. Box and point coordinates go through the random-effects decomposition
already inside `iaa/continuous.py`, which separates an annotator who
systematically draws bigger boxes (bias) from one who is noisy (variance).

Temporal agreement uses the same machinery in one dimension, and everything
that depends on a tolerance window is reported as a **sweep** rather than at a
single threshold. Annotators who agree to within two seconds may agree on
nothing at a quarter-second; quoting one number makes the claim
unfalsifiable. Flat across the sweep means they found the same instant.

This also fixed something that was quietly wrong. Adjudication compared the
*keys* of an annotation, and an image schema stores everything under one key
named `_data`, so **every image pair scored 1.0 agreement** — two annotators
who agreed on nothing looked unanimous, and no image was ever routed for
review. See [Geometry Agreement](../advanced/geometry_agreement.md).

## Vision: the surface works now

Several shipped vision features did not run. Accepting an AI detection called a
method that did not exist. The freeform tool drew paths that were never saved.
Masks leaked between instances, because masks are not fabric objects and every
canvas-scoped operation missed them — three separate instance-switch
corruption bugs in one method's blast radius.

Beyond the repairs:

- **Geometry primitives** — `polyline`, `keypoint_set` (COCO visibility flags
  and declared skeletons), `ellipse`, `cuboid_2d` and `tubelet`, each wired
  through the whole path from the tool list to the importers. COCO keypoints
  stop being import-only.
- **Instance-keyed masks** — two adjacent cats are two instances, not one
  blob. Bare label keys are read-coerced, so no migration.
- **Class visibility** — hide or solo a class with `h` / `Shift+H`, persisted
  per project rather than per file, and shared with video annotation.
- **Copy from the previous image** (`Ctrl/Cmd+D`), with `carry_over` for
  automatic pre-fill on items that have no annotations of their own.
- **Tablet support** — two-finger pan and pinch zoom. Panning was gated on
  Alt/Space, keyboard state a stylus annotator does not have, so zooming in
  stranded them.
- The mask/viewport transform is now one round-trip-tested function pair
  instead of two implementations that could disagree. They did, which is why
  masks drifted from the image under zoom.

## Segmentation, text prompts, and video tracking

`pip install potato` gives working interactive segmentation with no GPU, no new
Python dependency and no network. ONNX Runtime Web is vendored; `mobile_sam` is
the default.

- **Click to segment** — positive and negative points, box prompts, and
  refinement from a prior mask. Decode is under 100 ms and entirely local.
- **Text prompts** (Grounding DINO, Apache-2.0, in the browser) — type a
  phrase, get every match boxed as a suggestion. `wordpiece.js` implements BERT
  tokenization directly rather than pulling in 2 MB of transformers.js for one
  function, checked token-for-token against HuggingFace tokenizers. Quantization
  is `q4f16` on measurement: against the 686 MB full-precision export it holds
  box IoU 0.972 where int8 holds 0.874, and is 50 MB smaller.
- **Video mask propagation** (SAM 2, server-side) — draw a mask on one frame,
  propagate, correct any frame, re-propagate. Measured against known ground
  truth: per-frame IoU 0.974–0.979 with no decay, 1.32 s/frame on CPU. Occluded
  frames come back empty because the model reports occlusion itself.
- **SAM 3** is available as a licence-gated server endpoint. No weights are
  bundled and `download-models` refuses without `--accept-licence`.
- **`potato/model_zoo.py`** is the single registry behind all of it: task,
  licence, whether that licence needs explicit acceptance, requirements, and
  the parameters the browser needs. Adding a model is one entry plus one
  session class. See [Model Zoo](../ai-intelligence/model_zoo.md).

## Import and export formats

15 importers and 29 exporters. COCO (including crowd RLE, read as-is), YOLO,
Pascal VOC, CVAT, V7 Darwin, Labelbox, LabelMe, Cityscapes, KITTI,
MOTChallenge, DAVIS/YouTube-VOS, Open Images, HuggingFace, WebDataset and VIA.

`potato import` takes directories and zips, not just single files, and
auto-detects by signature file. [The format
matrix](../data-export/format_matrix.md) documents every format against every
capability with explicit lossiness, and a test asserts the table matches the
registries, so it cannot lie.

**Media ingest** handles what browsers cannot display: TIFF (multi-page and
16-bit, with a windowing control), HEIC and camera RAW transcode to WebP;
HEVC, ProRes, MKV and MOV get an ffmpeg proxy transcode with an
extracted-frames fallback. ffmpeg and Pillow-SIMD stay optional — missing them
produces the exact conversion command, never a broken player.

## Deep zoom

`viewer: deepzoom` builds one tile pyramid served as both DZI and IIIF Image
API 3.0, driven by OpenSeadragon (vendored). The arrangement is inverted from
the usual: fabric draws in image-pixel coordinates and OpenSeadragon transforms
the whole canvas, so coordinate conversion and normalization are correct
unmodified. The transform is read from the library, never recomputed —
recomputing it is wrong exactly mid-animation. **Masks work at the source's
full resolution**, which V7 documents as unsupported on tiled images.
See [Deep Zoom](../annotation-types/multimedia/deep_zoom.md).

## 3D, depth, and embodied episodes

- **Point clouds** — `spatial_annotation` with `cuboid_3d`, `point_3d`,
  `polyline_3d` and `segment_3d`. PCD, PLY, KITTI `.bin` and LAS readers;
  KITTI and nuScenes import and export. Calibration is first-class, so a 3D box
  projects into every camera image and annotators verify in 2D while editing in
  3D.
- **Octree level of detail**, on by default: each node keeps the points its
  ancestors did not claim, so a partially loaded cloud looks coarse rather than
  incomplete. This uncovered a live data bug — `segment_3d` stores point
  indices whose stability assumed a fixed decimation, but `max_points` is a
  schema option, so lowering it silently re-pointed every stored per-point
  label. Indices now refer to the source file.
- **Depth maps** — 16-bit PNG/TIFF, NPY, PFM and EXR with a near/far window,
  colormaps, an RGB underlay and a metres readout under the cursor. The readout
  is the point: an 8-bit colormap is not injective, and a depth map that is 30%
  short looks normal once the window rescales. Zero means "no return" and is
  painted magenta rather than treated as the nearest surface.
- **Orthographic slab views** — three axis-aligned panels below the viewport. A
  perspective projection compresses extent along the view axis, so boxes placed
  by eye come out short in depth and the error is invisible from the camera
  that drew them.
- **Embodied episodes** — `episode_annotation` renders N synchronized video
  streams plus M time series (joint positions, gripper state, force-torque,
  reward) on one timeline. Action-phase segmentation, success/failure with a
  cause taxonomy, dense progress-reward curves, hindsight instruction
  relabelling, and affordance points. Imports LeRobot v2, RLDS/TFDS, HDF5 and
  ROS bags; exports LeRobot v2 plus a JSONL sidecar that does not require
  rewriting the source dataset. See
  [Episodes](../annotation-types/embodied/episodes.md).

## World-model rollout evaluation

`rollout_evaluation` puts several videos of the same scenario side by side,
frame-locked on one timeline. The annotator finds the frame at which each
rollout stops making sense, tags why from a physics and consistency taxonomy,
picks a winner, and — where the scenario carries an intervention — judges
whether the divergence follows from it.

Rating a generated video 3/5 for "physical plausibility" produces a number that
cannot be checked or located. A frame plus a category can: a researcher opens
frame 47, the failure has a place in the tensor, and two annotators' answers
are two points on a line, so a chance-corrected statistic applies.

Three design decisions:

- **"No breaks" is an explicit act**, not the absence of marks. An unmarked
  panel is otherwise ambiguous between "watched it, nothing wrong" and "never
  got to it", and those give opposite detection agreements.
- **Panel order and blinding are decided server-side**, seeded from
  (annotator, item) so a revisit shows the same order. A client-side shuffle
  reshuffles on reload, and the annotator's second look disagrees with their
  first.
- **The frame rate is declared, never guessed.** HTML5 video exposes none, and
  a frame number off by 30/24 is worse than no frame number because it looks
  right. Without a declared rate, frame numbers are omitted.

See [World-Model Evaluation](../agent-evaluation/world_model_eval.md).

## VLM grounding and pointing

`grounding_eval` and `region_caption`, plus `potato/grounding/`. Grounding,
pointing and ungroundedness are scored separately, because a point has no area
and IoU against it is always 0. Grounding accuracy reports four thresholds
rather than one. Caption agreement needed no new coefficient, only a distance
over text — α already accepts a callable — and the default token distance is
documented as a poor proxy, with measured numbers, rather than sold as one.
See [VLM Grounding](../agent-evaluation/vlm_grounding.md).

## Model-in-the-loop

- **Vision active learning** — `potato/embedders/` puts one project-wide
  embedder behind a lazy registry, with text, image, audio, video and
  admin-supplied backends and modality detection from the items. Every existing
  query strategy (uncertainty, diversity, BADGE, BALD, hybrid) then works on
  images unchanged. The corpus map uses the same embedder, no longer requires
  `diversity_ordering`, and reports which backend, model and field produced the
  points.
- **VLM critique** — crop each annotated region, ask a vision model whether it
  contains what it claims, whether the boundary is tight, and what was missed.
  Renders as a review queue with rationales. This catches the failure IoU
  cannot: two annotators confidently agreeing on the wrong thing.
- **Drawing telemetry** — time per shape, vertex count against shape
  complexity, stroke dynamics, zoom behaviour, revision count, and
  AI-suggestion accept latency, which is how rubber-stamping shows up. Raw
  streams go to SQLite, never into `user_state.json`.

## Threaded conversations and ConvoKit, both ways

The `dialogue` display renders reply structure: set `indent_replies: true` and
nesting is derived from each turn's `reply_to`, with turn identity read from
`turn_id`, `step_id` or plain `id`, so forum exports, chat logs and mailing
lists work unchanged. Per-turn timestamps and metadata chips. One field
supports whole-thread schemes, per-comment radio/likert/select/text, spans, and
`span_link` between spans in different comments, all at once.
`conversation_tree` gains per-node widgets keyed by node id, so a branching
tree and a flat thread can refer to the same messages.

`potato convokit <corpus>` imports any [ConvoKit](https://convokit.cornell.edu/)
corpus by name, directory or zip, at conversation or utterance granularity, and
`--format convokit` exports back as corpus metadata — either `info.<field>.jsonl`
overlays or a full corpus dump. Each turn carries the real utterance id, so
per-comment annotations round-trip by lookup. Every format variant in the wild
is read, down to the pre-rename `user`/`root`/`users.json` layout. No
`convokit` dependency; the format is read and written with the standard library.
Also `--emit-config`, `--dry-run` and `--list-corpora`.
See [ConvoKit](../integrations/convokit.md).

## Keystroke logging and typing dynamics

Opt-in via `keystroke_logging.enabled`: content-blind capture of *how* a
free-text answer was produced, with composed / transcribed / pasted detection.
Capture keys on `beforeinput` and `InputEvent.inputType`, not `keydown` —
paste, drop, IME, dictation and autofill all mutate a field without firing
keydown, so a keydown-only logger is blind to exactly the cases this exists to
detect. The gap between characters that appeared and keys actually pressed is
the strongest single signal.

No pre-trained model ships. There is no labelled corpus here, and fitted
coefficients would be fabricated validation, so detection is six transparent
rules with visible evidence and per-project percentile calibration. Annotators
see a recording notice. See [Keystroke
Logging](../advanced/keystroke_logging.md) and the [ethics
note](../advanced/keystroke_logging_ethics.md).

## Live database ingestion (#166)

Database sources gain an optional background poller, so rows created after
startup become assignable within `poll_interval_seconds` with no restart. The
cursor is read from the raw row before datetimes are ISO-formatted, because
re-binding an ISO string against a Postgres `timestamptz` is unreliable, and
keyset predicates use the portable three-term OR rather than row-value
comparison, which SQL Server lacks.

## Specs coding agents can check

The hand-written API reference described 84 endpoints against 400+ registered
rules, and the YAML config — the actual product interface — had no contract at
all. Both are now generated from the registries the server validates against:

- `potato/schemas/potato-config.schema.json` — 159 config keys, 61 annotation
  types, 24 display types, plus per-type conditionals, so a `constant_sum`
  scheme is told it needs `labels` before the server rejects it.
- `docs/api-reference/openapi.json` — 419 paths and 456 operations, walked off
  the live Flask `url_map`, with config-gated blueprints registered onto scratch
  apps so they are not silently omitted, and per-endpoint auth recovered by an
  AST scan of the blueprint decorators.

CI fails when either drifts from the code. `mkdocs build --strict` also passes
now, on 24 repaired dead links and 15 invented anchors, and runs `--strict` in
the docs job so the rot cannot recur. See [Machine-Readable
Specs](../api-reference/machine_readable.md).

## Performance: the admin Instances tab

The tab was quadratic in the corpus. Building one page of 25 rows cost
instances × annotators × annotations, because each of three per-row helpers
walked every annotator and one of them rebuilt every annotation that annotator
had ever made.

| items (5 annotators) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 250 | 100 ms | 2 ms |
| 500 | 488 ms | 3 ms |
| 1,000 | 2.9 s | 9 ms |
| 2,000 | 15.1 s | 23 ms |
| 20,000 × 20 annotators | ~100 min (extrapolated) | 753 ms |

Correctness was checked against the old code over 60 query permutations —
identical, except for two columns that had never worked. The modal-label and
disagreement columns read a `label_name` attribute `Label` does not have, fell
through to `str(value)`, and counted `"True"` for everyone, so the modal label
was always `True` and disagreement was always 0.00.

## Offline and air-gapped installs

Every frontend asset now serves locally. jQuery, Bootstrap (JS and CSS), Font
Awesome, fabric.js and OpenSeadragon are vendored and checksum-verified against
the hashes their CDNs publish, across all 14 templates rather than only the
annotation page. That includes login, signup, password reset and error pages.

Three external hosts were undocumented, one of them a third-party favicon on
the login and signup pages: a request to another company from the page where
users type their credentials. `styles.css` also opened with an `@import` of
Google Fonts, which every existing guard was structurally blind to because they
scan template tags rather than stylesheet contents. Beyond breaking offline, it
sent each annotator's IP and user agent to Google on every page load, from a
tool people self-host so their data does not leave. A new guard covers CSS.
See [Air-Gapped Deployment](../deployment/air_gap.md).

## Packaging

`setup.py` declared package data as a single-level glob, `templates/*.html`, so
**every template in a subdirectory was missing from the wheel** — 27 files
covering solo mode's setup routes, the admin pages, judge calibration and the
corpus map. Anyone who `pip install`ed Potato hit it; anyone running from a
checkout never did, which is also why the test suite saw nothing. Reported and
fixed in [#164](https://github.com/davidjurgens/potato/pull/164) by
[@0x6362](https://github.com/0x6362).

The fix grafts the whole directory, with a prune for
`potato/templates/generated/` — runtime output that is gitignored, which
`MANIFEST.in` does not read, so a release built from a working tree would
otherwise carry the maintainer's own task templates. A test builds the real
manifest and fails if either half regresses.

## Other fixes

- **Single-select schemas could persist every value clicked**
  ([#167](https://github.com/davidjurgens/potato/issues/167)). The stale-label
  pre-clear keyed off a hardcoded `{'radio', 'multiselect'}` set, so `likert`
  kept both answers; on SurveyFlow pages every type accumulated, radio
  included. Exclusivity now comes from a `single_select` flag on the schema
  registry and is enforced at write time, so no route can bypass it. New
  `potato repair-annotations` rewrites already-corrupted state, resolving each
  answer from the timestamped change trail rather than stored order — the label
  dict serializes in first-touch order, so "last entry wins" answers wrongly.
- **Dialogue span offsets drifted.** The server collapsed whitespace while the
  client deliberately did not, so spans were sliced a few characters further
  off per turn: short conversations looked correct and long ones returned
  neighbouring text.
- **`getCurrentFrame` was off by one after every seek**, on every clip, for
  every annotator — `currentTime` comes back truncated to six decimal places,
  so frame 14 at 12 fps reads back as 13. Pre-existing, unrelated to tracking.
- **Rooms accepted any schema with a `labels` list**, which includes every
  image, video, audio and spatial class palette, and closing an item deleted
  that annotator's geometry and wrote a class name over it. `create_room` now
  classifies the schema and refuses.
- **Four subsystems were operating on filenames.** `Item.get_text()` returns an
  item's first string value when there is no text key, which on a media corpus
  is the instance id — so the corpus map plotted a UMAP of `img_01, img_02,
  …`, Boundary Lab tried to paraphrase `"img_01"`, search indexed the corpus's
  own ids, and rooms asked people to vote on `(no text)`.
- `onlyOne()` forced the clicked input checked, so an armed span code could
  never be disarmed and in-vivo coding was unreachable.
- `potato/export/cli.py` read data files line by line only, so a JSON-array
  data file exported zero items.
- `MysqlUserState` raised `AttributeError` on every save.
- `ConversationTreeDisplay` ignored its `display_options` block.
- `validate_cli` reported `FAILED — 0 error(s)` for configs that pass with
  warnings.
- Five video coordinate and frame bugs, including mask keyframes that rendered
  nothing because the overlay skipped any keyframe without a bbox.
- **`pip install 'potato[vision]'` installed nothing.** The extra was named in
  the docs and in the SAM endpoint's own error message, but was never declared
  in `setup.py`, so pip warned and moved on. It is now real. `segment-anything`
  is deliberately not in it, because Meta publishes it from GitHub and the PyPI
  name is an anonymous upload. The endpoint names the official source instead.
- `MANIFEST.in` referenced `potato/base_html/`, a directory that has not existed
  for years. It warned on every build.
- Boot no longer eagerly imports the ML stack; AI SDKs sit behind a lazy
  endpoint registry.

## Upgrading

**Image annotation keyboard shortcuts changed.** The defaults now follow the V7
conventions annotators arrive with: `b` brush, `r` rectangle, `f` fill, `k`
keypoint, `v` select, `[` / `]` size. Previously `b` was bbox and `f` was
freeform. **If you have a study collecting right now**, set
`keybinding_profile: legacy` on the schema to restore the old table exactly;
annotators under a rebound profile see a one-time notice listing what moved.

**Everything else is backward compatible.** Masks stored under bare label keys
are read as instance 0. No data migration is required for any of the geometry
or agreement work.

**New optional extras.** Vision models, embedders and media transcoding are
opt-in: `pip install potato[vision]`, and `potato download-models` fetches
weights on request. A default install adds no new required dependency.

URL: https://potatoannotator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/releasenotes/v2.7.1/

# Release Notes: v2.7.1 — Transcripts In, Without the Reformatting

A focused release for anyone arriving at Potato with speech already transcribed. Potato now reads **21 transcript and subtitle formats** directly — up from 6 — loads them from **sidecar files next to your media** instead of requiring every transcript to be inlined into your data JSON, and ships a `potato transcripts` converter for turning a directory of ASR output into a ready-to-annotate data file. All four transcript-consuming schemas now accept the same formats.

Everything here is pure standard library. No new dependencies, and ASR and diarization still run upstream of Potato — it reads what your pipeline produced, it does not transcribe.

## 21 input formats

**ASR output** — Whisper JSON, WhisperX / diarized JSON, whisper.cpp JSON, Whisper TSV, AWS Transcribe, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Rev.ai, SPoRC.

**Subtitles and captions** — SubRip (`.srt`), WebVTT (`.vtt`), SubStation Alpha (`.ass`, `.ssa`), TTML / DFXP, YouTube `json3`, YouTube `srv1`/`srv2`/`srv3`.

**Forced alignment (import)** — NIST CTM, Praat TextGrid, ELAN EAF. EAF and TextGrid *export* already shipped, so tiered annotations now round-trip: import an existing alignment, correct it in Potato, export back to your ELAN or Praat workflow.

Detection is driven by the shape of the data, not the file extension, so inline transcripts keep working exactly as before. **Word-level timings and per-segment confidence are now preserved** where the source provides them; formats that are natively word-level (CTM, Deepgram, AssemblyAI) group words into turns on speaker change plus a pause threshold.

## Sidecar transcript files

A transcript no longer has to be pasted into your data file. Point at it:

```json
{"id": "int_001", "conversation": {"audio": "media/int_001.mp3", "transcript": "media/int_001.srt"}}
```

Paths resolve relative to `task_dir` and are validated against directory traversal. A display option `transcript_is_path: auto | true | false` overrides the heuristic when inline text happens to look like a path.

## `potato transcripts` — bulk converter

```bash
potato transcripts ./whisper_out --media-dir ./audio -o data/interviews.json
potato transcripts ./captions --media-url-prefix https://cdn.example.org/ -o data/talks.json --emit-config
```

Globs a directory of transcripts, pairs each to its media by basename (or builds a URL), derives item ids from filenames, and writes a Potato data file. `--dry-run` reports the detected format, turn count, and speakers found per file without writing anything — which is also the diagnostic to reach for when a transcript renders as one undifferentiated bubble.

## One format vocabulary across four schemas

`audio_dialogue`, `speech_transcript`, `voice_interaction`, and `tiered_annotation` previously each parsed transcript data their own way and accepted different subsets of formats for no stated reason. They now share the normalizer through a server-side `_transcripts` index attached at render time, so whatever one accepts, all four accept. Existing configs are unaffected — each schema keeps its prior parsing as a fallback.

`tiered_annotation` additionally gains opt-in **transcript seeding** (`transcript_field`, `transcript_tier`): a tier is pre-populated from the transcript so annotators correct an existing alignment instead of re-segmenting from scratch. Seeded intervals are not auto-saved — they become annotations only when the annotator touches them, so an untouched seed is never misattributed as human work.

## Documentation

- **[Transcript & Subtitle Formats](../annotation-types/multimedia/transcript_formats.md)** — the reference: every format with its detection rule and what it contributes, the normalized turn model, sidecar rules, all config keys, an explicit *not supported* list, and troubleshooting keyed to real symptoms.
- **[Working with Transcripts](../guides/working_with_transcripts.md)** — the task guide, with two entry paths that converge: *"I ran Whisper on my audio"* and *"I have YouTube subtitles."*
- `audio_annotation.md`, `video_annotation.md`, `audio_dialogue.md`, and `export_formats.md` updated and cross-linked. `audio_dialogue.md` was linked from the docs index but missing from the mkdocs nav entirely — now fixed, along with the missing v2.7.0 nav entry.
- New example: `examples/audio/transcript-formats/`, six formats side by side over sidecar paths.

## Fixes

- **`user_input()` / `user_input_leave()` ReferenceError.** The instance-jump input in the base templates wired `onfocusin`/`onfocusout` to two functions that are not defined anywhere in the codebase, throwing two console exceptions every time an annotator focused the box. Removed from all five affected templates. `front_end.py` matches that exact markup to implement `allow_jumping_to_id: false`, so both of its replacement strings were updated in lockstep.

## Upgrade

```bash
pip install --upgrade potato-annotation==2.7.1
```

No configuration changes are required. Every previously accepted transcript shape is still accepted, byte-for-byte.

<!-- source: docs/releasenotes/v2.7.0.md -->
URL: https://potatoannotator.readthedocs.io/en/latest/releasenotes/v2.7.0/

# Release Notes: v2.7.0 — Seven New Ways to Annotate

The largest Potato release yet: 342 files changed, ~50,000 lines added, 33 commits since v2.6.2. It has two halves. The first is a wave of seven new opt-in features — Psychometrics, Multiplayer Rooms, Boundary Lab, Truth Serum, Think-Aloud Mode, Paper Mode, and Pocket Mode — built around one idea: an annotation tool should not just *collect* labels, it should measure how labels come to be, and the process itself should produce more than point labels. None of the seven requires an LLM. The second half is a broad workflow-and-infrastructure wave: cross-document event annotation, turn-level annotation, CoT process-reward labeling, PDF cross-page linking, a living-document codebook, RBAC roles with per-cohort schemas, localized dashboards in 10 languages, and a much lighter core install.

## Psychometrics Engine — labels with error bars

A live item-response-theory layer (multiclass GLAD; no gold labels, no LLM) that refits in milliseconds as labels stream in, jointly estimating each annotator's ability and each item's difficulty from agreement patterns alone.

- **Every exported label carries a posterior and confidence interval** — `p = 0.94 [0.88–0.97]` instead of a bare majority vote (`/psychometrics/api/export`).
- **`assignment_strategy: psychometric`** routes each item to whichever annotator's judgment carries the most expected information, and items past the confidence threshold **stop consuming annotation budget** (the dashboard shows judgments and dollars saved).
- **Codebook-bug detector** — items where your *best* annotators disagree most (negative discrimination) are flagged: that pattern means the item is broken, not the people.
- **Pre-study power analysis** — `python -m potato.psychometrics.design` recommends annotators-per-item for a target Krippendorff-α precision via Monte Carlo, with cost estimates.
- Live dashboard at `/psychometrics/dashboard`; example in `examples/advanced/psychometrics/`. See [Psychometrics](../advanced/psychometrics.md).

## Multiplayer Rooms — live norming sessions, measured

Synchronized group annotation at `/rooms`: the calibration meetings teams already run over screen-share, made part of the tool and instrumented. Rooms sync by cursor-polling an event stream — no WebSockets, no new dependencies.

- **Norming rooms** — everyone votes blind (enforced server-side: pre-reveal, nobody can see another member's label, only who has voted) → the host reveals → the group discusses in a side chat → anyone may change their vote. Blind votes are immutable after the reveal; every post-reveal change is logged with the majority at that moment — a per-member **conformity record**.
- **Live agreement meter** — Krippendorff's α computed twice over revealed items: blind votes vs current votes. The gap is the session's *norming lift* — whether the meeting was worth it, on screen while it happens.
- **Huddles** — one click seeds a room from every item the team currently disagrees on, with the original annotations shown as context: adjudication as a conversation.
- **Shadow rooms** — trainees join as observers and watch the host's votes, reveals, and text selections live.
- **Event-sourced** — every room appends to `rooms/room-<CODE>.jsonl`; state is a pure replay, so live rooms survive restarts and the log is the session's audit trail. Final votes persist into members' regular annotation state. See [Multiplayer Rooms](../advanced/multiplayer_rooms.md).

## Boundary Lab — annotate the boundary, not the point

The moment an annotator commits a label, Potato shows minimal counterfactual edits of the text and asks: *you said Polite — would that survive this edit?* One click per probe. Ordinary annotation then produces contrast sets for free (every answered probe is a labeled original/counterfactual pair, à la Gardner et al. 2020), boundary rationales that pinpoint codebook ambiguity, and invisible quality control (annotators who flip on meaning-preserving paraphrases get flagged — no fake gold items planted). Rule-based generation, no LLM. See [Boundary Lab](../advanced/boundary_lab.md).

## Truth Serum — surprisingly-popular scoring

After each label, one micro-question: *what percentage of other annotators will agree with you?* Those predictions power the surprisingly-popular estimator (Prelec et al. 2017, Nature): the label whose actual popularity most exceeds its predicted popularity beats majority vote exactly where annotation is hard — no gold labels required. The dashboard's *"where the crowd is likely wrong"* queue surfaces items to review first, plus per-annotator calibration scores. To our knowledge the first annotation tool to ship peer-prediction scoring. See [Truth Serum](../advanced/truth_serum.md).

## Think-Aloud Mode — voice rationales, zero LLM

Annotators just *talk* while they work. Speech-to-text runs fully locally (faster-whisper, CPU real-time on the 39 MB `tiny.en` model); the verbatim transcript is stored as the rationale — deliberately un-summarized, because paraphrasing a think-aloud protocol contaminates the artifact. Labels can be committed by voice ("I'd call it neutral", "final answer: polite") via a rule-based parser. Nothing leaves the machine. See [Think-Aloud Mode](../advanced/think_aloud.md).

## Paper Mode — the dataset that writes its own methods section

```bash
python -m potato.paper config.yaml -o paper_export
```

One command turns a Potato project into a compilable LaTeX dataset report: dataset description, label distributions, annotator table, agreement statistics with the right citations (`paper.bib` included), timing, and a limitations paragraph. Every section sits between cut-paste markers; tables also export as CSV and every number as JSON. Fully offline, no LLM, no server. See [Paper Mode](../advanced/paper_mode.md).

## Mobile annotation (Pocket Mode)

Potato now supports phones and tablets as first-class annotation devices. With `pocket: {enabled: true}`, touch devices that open the task are **detected and routed automatically** to a mobile interface — a card stack with thumb-zone label buttons, swipe navigation, offline annotation with automatic sync, and home-screen installation as a PWA. For single-radio tasks, one tap = one labeled item. Detection is two-layer (server-side User-Agent plus a client-side primary-pointer check that catches iPads masquerading as Macs), with a sticky "Desktop site" opt-out.

Not every annotation type is mobile friendly: tasks that include desktop-only schemas (spans, bounding boxes, video...) are never degraded onto touch — phones keep the desktop UI and see a dismissible warning that a desktop browser is recommended. Either way, a new **Devices tab in the admin dashboard** shows who is annotating from what (mobile/tablet/desktop visit counts per user, tracked whether or not Pocket Mode is enabled), so you can spot phone annotators on desktop-only tasks. See [Mobile Annotation](../advanced/pocket_mode.md).

## Try them together

`examples/advanced/showcase/` runs one politeness task with five of the new features enabled at once — probes, peer predictions, voice rationales, live psychometrics, and a one-command paper export.

## Cross-document event annotation + corpus map

Annotate **events that span many documents**. Instead of labeling one document at a time, annotators build *events* — first-class records that aggregate evidence from across a corpus into a shared template (event type, participants, location, time), the way cross-document event corpora (ECB+, GVC, ERE) are actually constructed.

- New `multi_document_event` schema wired through config and blueprints, backed by a **cross-document event registry**.
- **Corpus map** — an ingest pipeline plus an annotator navigation API for moving through a corpus by event rather than by document.
- Annotator UI for citing evidence into event slots; unit, server, and Selenium coverage; a runnable disaster-news corpus example. See [Multi-Document Events](../advanced/multi_document_events.md).

## Turn-level annotation & multi-agent traces

Apply any annotation scheme **per turn** of a conversation or agent trace instead of once per instance. Schemes bind to declarative filters — by speaker, agent, step type, tool name, or turn range — and render inline inside every matching turn, with values stored under stable turn ids. This generalizes the dialogue display's `per_turn_ratings` to multiple display types and all widget types. Alongside it: a **multi-agent discussion display** with agent identity tracking and a **run tree**, plus a review workflow for session-level annotation. See [Turn-Level Annotation](../agent-evaluation/turn_level_annotation.md).

## Chain-of-thought process-reward annotation

Turn a long CoT reasoning trace into a vertical list of reviewable steps, have an external LLM pre-score each step (correct / neutral / incorrect), and let a human confirm or override each one — the standard "LLM labels, human verifies" pattern for producing **Process Reward Model (PRM)** training data much faster than labeling from scratch. Includes automatic CoT segmentation, the new `cot_trace` display, a `process_reward` scheme with per-step provenance (which labels came from the model, which were verified or overridden), and a pre-label API. See [Process Reward CoT](../agent-evaluation/process_reward_cot.md).

## PDF: cross-page linking + OCR

A new PDF **link mode**: place text-span and region-box anchors on any page and draw typed links between them **across pages** — anchors are unified span objects carrying page/bbox geometry. Optional OCR (`false`/`true`/`"auto"`) builds a text layer for scanned PDFs. PDF.js is now vendored, so PDF tasks work offline.

## Living codebook document

The codebook grows a full **living-document form**: a typed-block markdown document (definitions, examples, decision rules) with a full-page editor at `/codebook` and a distiller that keeps the document and the code list in sync. Codes remain first-class — add, rename, recolor, move, and delete without touching YAML. See [Codebook](../advanced/codebook.md).

## Teams, access control & assignment

- **RBAC roles** — role/permission-based access control; admin blueprints now route through it uniformly.
- **Per-cohort schemas** — different annotator cohorts can see different annotation schemes (or subsets), bound to the same cohorts used for batch assignment; the global scheme list remains the default and fallback. See [Per-Cohort Schemas](../advanced/per_cohort_schemas.md).
- **Automatic batch assignment for unknown annotators** (#163) — annotators who show up without a pre-assigned batch get one automatically, and auto-assigned cohort pins now persist across restarts.
- **Scaling guide** — a new deployment doc on how Potato actually behaves with large datasets and which knobs matter. See [Scaling](../deployment/scaling.md).

## Localization

Admin and annotator dashboards are localized, with **10 bundled languages**: Arabic, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, and Chinese.

## LLM endpoint plumbing

- `${ENV_VAR}` expansion inside LLM endpoint config blocks — keep API keys out of YAML.
- OpenAI-compatible `base_url` normalization for local/vLLM endpoints, and bare-host URL normalization before Playwright navigation in web-agent tasks.

## Packaging: lighter core install

- **AI SDKs are now imported lazily.** A core `pip install potato-annotation` no longer requires (or imports) any AI SDK: endpoints register as lazy specs and the SDK is imported only when a config selects that `endpoint_type`. Previously a core install could fail to boot with a missing-`ollama` error; now a missing SDK produces a clear message naming the exact `pip install` to run.
- **The `[ai]` extra now covers all first-party LLM endpoints** — `anthropic` and `google-genai` join `ollama` and `openai` (`pip install "potato-annotation[ai]"`).
- Server boot import time drops from ~2.0s to ~0.7s with SDKs installed, since none of them load at boot anymore.

## Paper & citation

Potato 2.0 has an official paper at **ACL 2026** (demo track). The README badge, official citation, and a `CITATION.cff` are included — if you use Potato in research, there is now a current reference to cite.

## Fixes & maintenance

- Repaired 7 pre-existing unit-test failures; the full suite (7,482 tests) passes.
- Upgraded the bundled vite from 5 to 7, resolving 5 Dependabot alerts.
- `cot_trace` added to the static display-type fallback list in config validation.
- Corrected the Gemini SDK package name in docs (`google-genai`, not the legacy `google-generativeai`).

## Upgrade

```bash
pip install --upgrade potato-annotation==2.7.0
```

# Release Notes: v2.6.2 — Agent-Evaluation Differentiation (D/E series) + Multi-Agent & Multimodal Annotation (M series)

Building on the v2.6.1 agentic-evaluation suite (G1–G10), this release pushes Potato
**beyond parity** with LangSmith/LabelBox into capabilities no open tool offers: a
clickable multi-agent interaction graph, cross-agent failure attribution,
multimodal-agent annotation surfaces, judge–human alignment with confidence intervals, and
reward/optimization export. **13 new annotation schemas**, new evaluators and analytics
dashboards, and a set of robustness fixes. Every new schema ships with unit + Selenium
persistence tests, a runnable example, and docs.

## New evaluators & judge tooling (D-series)

- **`rubric_dag`, `rag_triad`, `agent_as_judge`** evaluators. The RAG triad scores
  context relevance / groundedness / answer relevance; `rubric_dag` evaluates a
  dependency graph of criteria; `agent_as_judge` runs an agentic judge.
- **Judge robustness eval cards** — verbosity-bias, position-swap consistency, and
  **Expected Calibration Error (ECE)**.
- Hardened core judge JSON parsing to tolerate fenced/`<think>`-wrapped model output.

## Statistical rigor & consensus (D-series)

Bootstrap confidence intervals, Wilson intervals, paired significance tests,
**Dawid–Skene** (EM) consensus, judge-drift trend tracking, and trace analytics.

## Model arena (D-series)

Provider-agnostic multi-model arena with **Elo / Bradley–Terry** rankings and
**pairwise-preference (DPO) export**; persona-driven multi-turn user simulation.

## Curation, integrity & optimization (E-series)

- **Failure-mode discovery** — cosine k-means clustering of failures with LLM-labeled
  axes, surfaced on the Catalog.
- **LLM-cheating / low-effort detection** — Correlated-Agreement + LLM-echo signals on
  a new **annotation-integrity** dashboard.
- **Perspectivist export** — soft-label distributions that preserve disagreement.
- **Reward export & optimization** — Rubrics-as-Rewards export, active-preference
  sampling, automatic metric induction, and a prompt-optimization (eval→improve) loop.

## Multi-agent team annotation (M-series) — new

Annotate the *team structure*, not just a flat transcript:

- **`agent_interaction_graph`** — a clickable directed graph (nodes = agents, edges =
  handoffs); mark the critical path and flag problematic edges. *(No open competitor
  offers this.)*
- **`failure_attribution`** — responsible agent + decisive step + reason (Who&When).
- **`handoff_review`** — every agent→agent handoff as an annotatable object with
  inter-agent-misalignment flags + quality.
- **`agent_scorecard`** — per-agent role fidelity / contribution / coordination, team
  dimensions, and milestones (MultiAgentBench-style).
- **`tool_contention`** — per-agent lanes of concurrent tool calls; flag deadlock /
  race / shared-resource collisions.
- **`emergent_behavior`** — tag turn-sets spanning agents for collusion / groupthink /
  cascading errors / role drift.
- **Recipes:** MAST-at-step (the 14 MAST modes on `trajectory_eval`) and
  orchestration-pattern confirmation.

See [Multi-Agent Team Annotation](../agent-evaluation/multi_agent_annotation.md).

## Multimodal-agent annotation (M-series) — new

For agents that drive GUIs, watch video, or hold spoken conversations:

- **`gui_trajectory`** — per-step screenshot + action with click-grounding (OSWorld /
  ScreenSpot / AndroidWorld).
- **`voice_interaction`** — dual-track (user/agent) timeline with barge-in/overlap
  classification (Full-Duplex-Bench).
- **`temporal_grounding`** — mark gold event intervals on video with a live **IoU** vs.
  the model's prediction (ET-Bench / TimeScope).
- **`speech_transcript`** — per-segment ASR/TTS/pronunciation/disfluency tagging with
  inline correction.
- **`multimodal_reasoning`** — rate each step of an interleaved text↔image↔tool trace
  for coherence and visual hallucination.
- **`tool_call_review`** — per-tool-call correctness (right tool / args / order;
  BFCL / MCPMark).
- **`table_grid`** — document-table cell-structure annotation (OmniDocBench /
  RealHiTBench).

See [Multimodal-Agent Annotation](../agent-evaluation/multimodal_agent_annotation.md).

## Fixes

- **`agent_interaction_graph`** — persist edge classification before re-render so the
  restore path can't clobber an in-progress edge cycle.
- **`trajectory_eval`** — tolerate plain-string / `label`-keyed `error_types` instead of
  raising an opaque `'str' object has no attribute 'get'` (which `safe_generate_layout`
  silently turned into an error block).
- **`table_grid`** — compact, table-like cells (previously `aspect-ratio:1/1` ballooned
  them in wide containers).
- **Examples** — restore the missing data file for the interaction-graph example, and
  add an integrity guard test that runs the real boot-time data-file validation (which
  the preview CLI skips) across all agent-eval examples.

## Reliability — trace & span round-trip integrity

- **Span serialization data loss fixed.** On save→reload, spans silently lost
  `target_field`, `id`, knowledge-base entity links (`kb_id`/`kb_source`/`kb_label`),
  discontinuous-span `additional_parts`, and `format_coords` — the on-disk serializer
  wrote fewer fields than the loader read. This broke multi-field span rendering across
  sessions. Both serializers now delegate to `SpanAnnotation.to_dict()` as the single
  source of truth.
- **Export CLI span crash fixed.** The CLI treated stored span data as a dict and
  crashed on `.items()`; it now correctly parses the list-of-`[span, value]` pairs into
  the schema-keyed shape every exporter expects (with legacy-dict fallback).
- **Round-trip regression suites added** for spans/links/events and for the full agent
  **trace import → store → export** pipeline: `CanonicalTrace` fidelity with a drift
  guard, per-importer auto-detection and normalization, the capture-SDK payload path,
  and real example-trace data.

## Annotator progress dashboard (opt-in, read-only) — new

An optional `/progress` page lets annotators see their own progress plus project-level
totals, without exposing admin actions or other annotators' identities. **Off by
default**; enable with an `annotator_dashboard` config block. Project stats are computed
by a shared helper reused by the admin Overview tab. Accessible (progressbar ARIA,
live regions, keyboard-friendly) and resilient (request timeout, graceful empty states).
See [Annotator Progress Dashboard](../administration/annotator_dashboard.md).

## Notes

- The agent-eval datasets package remains `potato.eval_datasets` (not `datasets`) to
  avoid shadowing the HuggingFace `datasets` library on the import path.
- Potato now ships **53 annotation schema types**, all free and open-source.

# Release Notes: v2.6.1 — Agentic Evaluation Suite (G1–G10)

This release builds out a full **agent-evaluation loop** on top of Potato's
annotation core, closing the gaps identified against LangSmith and LabelBox.
It adds programmatic evaluators, versioned datasets & experiments, a tracing SDK,
an automation-rules engine, pytest CI gating, automated judge calibration,
span/free-text judging, semantic curation, and a multi-model arena — capture →
automate → curate → evaluate → gate → calibrate, end to end. Every feature ships
with tests, docs, a runnable example, and admin UI.

## Programmatic evaluators (`potato.evaluators`)

A Flask-free, dependency-light evaluator library usable in the server, CI, and
the automation engine: deterministic **trajectory match** (strict/unordered/
subset/superset with per-tool argument matching), **tool-use** correctness,
**reference-free LLM-judge**, and heuristics (exact/contains/regex/edit-distance/
JSON/embedding). Optional lazy adapter for the MIT `agentevals` package. See
[Programmatic Evaluators](../agent-evaluation/evaluators.md).

## Datasets & Experiments (`potato.eval_datasets`, `potato.experiments`)

First-class **versioned datasets** (snapshot-per-mutation, tags, `as_of`, splits)
behind a pluggable `file`/`sqlite` store, and **experiments** that score a
dataset version with evaluators and compare runs over time. Curate examples from
loaded instances, ingested traces, or aggregated human annotations; export to
SFT/DPO. Admin UI + the eval inspect/control API (`/admin/eval/*`, including
assignment pause/resume). See [Datasets & Experiments](../agent-evaluation/datasets_and_experiments.md).

## Tracing SDK (`potato_trace`)

A lightweight, top-level `@traceable` decorator + context manager (sync & async)
that captures nested run trees and ships them to Potato's ingestion webhook, plus
an optional OpenTelemetry exporter. Dependency-light — importing it never pulls
Flask. See [Tracing SDK](../integrations/tracing_sdk.md).

## Automation rules engine (`potato.automation`)

A programmable `filter → sampling rate → actions` engine over every item entering
Potato (loaded or runtime-ingested). Actions route items to the annotation queue,
curate them into datasets, run evaluators, fire outbound webhooks, or notify
annotators (heavy actions run on a background worker; sampling is deterministic).
The generic webhook normalizer now carries through `status`/`feedback`/`score`/
`tags` so triage and automation rules can match those signals. See
[Automation Rules](../agent-evaluation/automation_rules.md).

## CI evaluation (`potato.testing`)

A pytest plugin (`@pytest.mark.potato_eval`, the `potato_eval` fixture, and an
`expect(...)` assertion API) that runs evaluations in your own test suite and
**fails the build on score-threshold regressions** (`--potato-threshold`), with
optional experiment recording. Registered via a `pytest11` entry point. See
[CI Evaluation](../agent-evaluation/ci_evaluation.md).

## Judge: automated calibration + span/free-text (`judge_alignment`)

- **Auto-calibration** — instances where a human corrected the judge become
  few-shot examples (leakage-guarded), re-run under a new prompt version, with
  base-vs-new κ reported.
- **Beyond categorical** — the judge now scores **span** (IoU-F1 vs human spans)
  and **free-text** (rubric dimensions: continuous/boolean/categorical) outputs,
  not just radio/likert.

See [Judge Alignment](../agent-evaluation/judge_alignment.md).

## `eval_trace` span annotation

The three-pane reasoning | function-calls | final-answer display is now
**span-annotatable** (`span_target: true`) for fine-grained error localization,
via the shared multi-field span pipeline. See [eval_trace](../agent-evaluation/eval_trace.md).

## Semantic curation / Catalog (`potato.curation`)

An embedding index (lazy, pluggable; no ML import at startup) powering
**similarity search** ("find traces like this failure") and **dynamic slices** —
saved semantic + metadata filters that auto-include new matching traces and
curate into datasets. See [Semantic Curation](../agent-evaluation/semantic_curation.md).

## Model arena (`potato.arena`)

Fan one prompt out to **N models side by side** (provider-agnostic via
`AIEndpointFactory`), compare responses, pick the best, and track a win-rate
leaderboard. One model failing never aborts the others. See
[Model Arena](../agent-evaluation/model_arena.md).

## HuggingFace Spaces, models & docs

A manifest-driven [HuggingFace Spaces deploy toolkit](../data-export/huggingface_spaces.md)
(build/deploy demo Spaces from `spaces_manifest.yaml` + 10 demo projects), a new
[Using HuggingFace Models](../ai-intelligence/huggingface_models.md) guide, a Hub
round-trip section in [HuggingFace export](../data-export/huggingface_export.md),
and accessibility/chrome polish (focus rings, larger nav targets).

## Notes

- New config blocks: `datasets`, `automation`, `curation`, `arena` — see the
  [config reference](../configuration/config_reference.md#agent-evaluation-suite).
- The agent-eval datasets package is `potato.eval_datasets` (not `datasets`) to
  avoid shadowing the HuggingFace `datasets` library on the import path.

# Release Notes: v2.6.0 — QDA Mode, LLM-as-Judge Calibration & Trajectory Editing

This release brings Potato into full qualitative-data-analysis (QDA) territory and deepens its agent-evaluation toolkit. It adds an interactive QDA Mode (universal persistence, memos, search, a living codebook, and cases), an LLM-as-judge calibration/alignment workflow with a signal-based triage queue, and trajectory-editing schemas for producing SFT/DPO training data. It also relicenses Potato to GPL-3.0-or-later and lands a large robustness wave. 84 commits since v2.5.0.

## Qualitative Data Analysis (QDA) Mode

A new opt-in `qda_mode` that turns Potato into a collaborative qualitative-coding environment. Enabling it auto-cascades sensible defaults (codebook open, memos on, cases on).

- **Universal SQLite persistence** — a shared project database underpins the new QDA surfaces (memos, search index, codebook, cases) alongside the existing annotation store.
- **Memos** — analyst memos with a sidebar UI, REST API, and a dedicated exporter flag, so reflective notes live next to the data.
- **Universal FTS5 search & claim** — full-text search across instances with an annotator search-and-claim sidebar; admin search and a claim guard prevent double-work.
- **Living codebook + cases (QDA Phase 1)** — a universal codebook with case grouping.
  - **In-vivo coding** — create a code straight from a text selection.
  - **On-the-fly add** — add codes in place with an in-form reconcile and a review worklist.
  - **Retroactive curation** — append-only merge/split of codes with an LLM propose-confirm flow.
  - **Revision provenance & versioning** — the codebook bumps a revision on any change, with a lightweight `/version` poll so clients pick up edits; provenance is tracked as an overlay separate from prompt-facing records.
- **Docs & examples** — see [QDA Mode](../advanced/qda.md); a composed `qda-mode` example plus per-feature example READMEs are included.

## Agent Evaluation & LLM-as-Judge

- **LLM-as-judge auto-labeling + blind human calibration** — auto-label trajectories with an LLM judge, then calibrate against blind human judgments to measure and tune trustworthiness. See [Judge Calibration](../ai-intelligence/judge_calibration.md).
- **Judge↔human alignment + signal-based triage queue** — quantify judge/human agreement and route the most informative items to humans first via a signal-based triage queue. See [Judge Alignment](../agent-evaluation/judge_alignment.md) and [Triage Queue](../agent-evaluation/triage_queue.md).
- **`eval_trace` display** — a three-pane agent-trace display for continuous evaluation. See [eval_trace](../agent-evaluation/eval_trace.md).
- **Trajectory editing schemas** — `trajectory_edit` and `trajectory_correction` for capturing edited/corrected agent trajectories as SFT/DPO training data. See [Trajectory Correction](../agent-evaluation/trajectory_correction.md).
- **Coding-agent eval** — `openai_tool_use` coding backend, a fixed coding-agent eval pipeline and web trace-review UI, and agentic display defect fixes surfaced by screenshot/live verification.

## Annotation Workflow & Assignment

- **Heterogeneous coverage** — per-item annotator caps, IAA reporting, and adjudication routing for tasks where items need different numbers of annotators.
- **Reclaim abandoned assignments** — recover annotation assignments abandoned by Prolific or QC-blocked workers, with configurable retention policies and idempotent, transaction-isolated reclaim.
- **Custom Batch assignment strategy** (#160) — assign predefined batches of items to specific annotators.
- **Phase page ordering** — order pages within a phase from configuration; phase type is now inferred from the canonical phase name (#154).
- **Reverse-proxy URL prefixes** — serve Potato under a sub-path behind a reverse proxy (#161).

## Licensing

- **Relicensed to GPL-3.0-or-later** (from PolyForm Shield). `setup.py`, `LICENSE`, and the README badge all reflect the change.

## Performance & Robustness

A large QA-hardening wave (F-022 through F-051):

- **Boot performance** — the ML stack is no longer eager-loaded at server boot (F-051): import time ~6.5s→2s, 50k-item boot ~10s→5.7s, RSS ~750→365MB.
- **Schema rename** — `annotation_type: highlight` → `span` with a migration (F-050).
- **Dynamic sources** — ingested traces are now assignable to annotators under the dynamic-source quota (F-037); `data_directory`/`data_sources`-only configs validate correctly (F-038).
- **Route registration** — registered 14 previously-dead admin/API routes and added an invariant test (F-042); registered the test `reset_state` route and stabilized the video-persistence suite (F-041).
- **Training phase** — fixed the `__main__`/module-split 404 and wired the all-phases example (F-043/F-044).
- **Prolific & payloads** — fixed the Prolific `__main__`-split (F-045) and hardened `/updateinstance` against non-dict payloads (F-046).
- **Persistence** — persist display-based bounding boxes for document/PDF displays (F-040); stop `populateInputValues` clobbering restored runtime codebook codes.
- **Export & survey** — stop silently dropping survey/phase responses (F-047); don't title-case author-written survey/consent labels (F-049).
- **Webhooks** — fixed four save-path bugs (500 on save, miswired events).
- **Solo mode** — backend fixes (B1–B7), UI polish, and fixed prompt optimization (F-022) so the optimizer is constructed and errors are no longer masked.
- **Active learning** — LLM cold-start honors nested `llm` config and tolerates fenced JSON.
- **Search UX** — matched terms highlight with `<mark>` instead of literal brackets.

pip install --upgrade potato-annotation==2.6.0

# Release Notes: v2.4.4 — Span Annotation Fixes & UX Improvements

Bug-fix release that resolves span overlay misalignment issues affecting all span annotation tasks, plus a small UX improvement for single-label span schemas.

## Bug Fixes

### Span Overlay Positioning Fix
- **Fixed overlays rendering on the wrong line of text.** The root cause was `white-space: pre-wrap` on `#text-content` being inherited by the `#span-overlays` container. Template whitespace inside `#span-overlays` was rendered as real content, causing absolutely-positioned overlays (which lacked explicit `top`/`left`) to use a "hypothetical static position" shifted ~30px down — exactly one line height. On multi-line text, overlays appeared on a completely different line than the selected text.
- **Fixed `collectTextNodes` walking into overlay containers.** The text-node walker in `getPositionsFromOffsets`, `getTextPositions`, and `getOffsetsFromSelection` recursed into `#span-overlays` children, causing overlay label text ("News", delete button "x") to inflate cumulative character offsets. Each successive span rendered at a progressively worse position.
- **Fixed `createSpanWithAlgorithm` using fragile `indexOf`-based positioning.** The initial span overlay was positioned using `getTextPositions()` which ignored the provided character offsets and searched `data-original-text` with `indexOf(text)` instead. When `data-original-text` differed from DOM text (e.g., after `loadAnnotations` overwrites it with normalized API text), the `indexOf` result pointed to wrong positions. Now uses `getPositionsFromOffsets()` (offset-based DOM walk) consistently, matching the reload rendering path.

### Python Compatibility
- Fixed Python 3.9 compatibility: replaced `match`/`case` with `if`/`elif` in `ai_cache.py`

### Other Fixes
- Added `__main__.py` to enable `python -m potato` execution
- Fixed marker registry, conversation-tree bug, and KeyError scope (PR #142)

## New Features

### Auto-Select Single Span Label
When a span schema has exactly one label, it is now automatically selected on page load. Annotators can immediately start highlighting text without needing to click the label checkbox first. Multi-label span schemas are unaffected and still require explicit selection. The checkbox remains visible and can be unchecked to disable span annotation mode.

## Upgrade

```bash
pip install --upgrade potato-annotation==2.4.4
```
